original_value: This work is focused on latent-variable graphical models for multivariate time series. We show how an algorithm which was originally used for finding zeros in the inverse of the covariance matrix can be generalized such that to identify the sparsity pattern of the inverse of spectral density matrix. When applied to a given time series, the algorithm produces a set of candidate models. Various information theoretic (IT) criteria are employed for deciding the winner. A novel IT criterion, which is tailored to our model selection problem, is introduced. Some options for reducing the computational burden are proposed and tested via numerical examples. We conduct an empirical study in which the algorithm is compared with the state-of-the-art. The results are good, and the major advantage is that the subjective choices made by the user are less important than in the case of other methods.

result.paraphrase: This work addresses latent-variable graphical models for multivariate time series. We demonstrate how an algorithm first used to find zeros in the inverse covariance matrix can be extended to identify the sparsity pattern of the inverse spectral density matrix. When run on a given time series, it yields a collection of candidate models. Several information-theoretic criteria are used to select the best one. We introduce a new IT criterion specifically designed for our model-selection problem. We also propose and test options for reducing computational cost through numerical examples. An empirical study compares the algorithm with the state of the art. The results are strong, and its main benefit is that user subjective choices matter less than they do with other methods.
